title: Deep Learning
short: Developing novel architectures and training paradigms for complex data.
detail: My work in deep learning focuses on architectures and training methods that remain efficient and reliable as data grows messier and models grow larger.
questions:
How can attention scale to long contexts without quadratic cost?
Which training signals make models robust to noisy or scarce labels?
How do we get calibrated uncertainty from deep networks?

title: Natural Language Processing
short: Building models that understand, generate, and reason with human language.
detail: I study how language models reason, where that reasoning breaks, and how to make small models competitive, including for low-resource languages like Bangla.
questions:
Can fine-tuning on intermediate thoughts improve factual consistency?
How well does knowledge transfer across languages with little data?
How do we evaluate reasoning beyond final-answer accuracy?

title: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
short: Enabling machines to perceive and interpret the visual world with high fidelity.
detail: In vision I work on recognition systems that generalize to new domains, from street scenes to medical images, with a focus on what models actually see.
questions:
Why do vision models fail under distribution shift?
How can semantic structure guide contrastive learning?
What makes dense prediction transfer well from pretraining?

title: MLOps & Deployment
short: Building scalable, reliable, and reproducible ML systems in production.
detail: Research only matters if it ships. I build tooling for reproducible training, evaluation and deployment so results hold up outside the lab.
questions:
How do we make large training runs deterministic and auditable?
What should continuous evaluation look like for ML models?
How do we monitor models for silent failure after deployment?
